2_Introduction: The device achieved a remarkable PCE of 17.0915%, with a VOC of 1.1067 V, JSC of 22.139 mA/cm², and FF of 69.7578%. The precursor solutions for all Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 films were prepared by dissolving equimolar concentrations (1.73 mol/L). A two-tier spin-coating strategy (1000 rpm/10 s and 5000 rpm/40 s) produced a uniform and defect-minimized perovskite layer. The crystallization process was refined by injecting 160 µL of antisolvent at last 10 s during spin-coating. The deposited perovskite films were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—engineered with a precisely tuned A-site cationic composition (FA⁺ dominant, supplemented by MA⁺ and Cs⁺ to optimize Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and suppress δ-phase formation while mitigating halide vacancy-mediated ion migration)—undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization via a two-tier spin-coating protocol that first ensures homogeneous precursor wetting at low speed (1000 rpm/10 s) and then drives rapid solvent extraction and nucleation confinement at high speed (5000 rpm/40 s), where the timed antisolvent quench (160 µL injected at the final 10 s) critically arrests Ostwald ripening, promotes uniform nucleation density, and suppresses pinhole formation by modulating supersaturation decay; this refined crystallization pathway yields large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary area, minimized non-radiative recombination centers (particularly undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at surfaces and interfaces), and enhanced phase purity—as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and sharp, narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection indicative of low microstrain and high crystallinity—while optical and PL mapping data reveal spatially homogeneous film coverage (>99.2% continuity), uniformly elevated photoluminescence intensity (3.8× enhancement vs. control), and monoexponential decay kinetics with τ₁ = 328 ns, collectively evidencing suppressed trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative channel preservation across the entire active area; the resulting structural integrity, interfacial homogeneity, and defect passivation synergistically enable balanced charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and robust operational stability, culminating in a VOC of 1.1067 V, JSC of 22.139 mA/cm², FF of 69.7578%, and PCE of 17.0915%.
